feed.title: Purplelink blog
feed.subtitle: Notes from a one-person studio making tools for academic researchers.

entry.title: Where Your Academic Record Actually Lives
entry.summary: Academics maintain their professional history in a dozen scattered places. When tenure reviews, grant applications, and annual reviews arrive, reconstructing the record from scratch is the problem.

entry.title: My travel photographs, now available as prints
entry.summary: About 500 travel and landscape photographs from the Alps, Japan, Iceland and more are now for sale as prints, plus the metadata bug that cut 65 titles short.

entry.title: Both bugs had the same symptom: zero
entry.summary: Building GlobePin's App Store analytics pipeline, I wrote code that treated absent data and broken requests identically. Two independent bugs, each enough to return nothing, sat undetected until Apple generated its first real reports.

entry.title: TikZ diagrams and tables in ModernTex, without writing either by hand
entry.summary: ModernTex now has a visual TikZ designer with live preview, and a Table Editor that pastes straight from Excel — both still write plain LaTeX underneath.

entry.title: Checking your response letter before resubmission
entry.summary: A response letter can address every reviewer comment without actually resolving the underlying concern. This is how a researcher uses Response to Reviewers to check that gap before resubmitting.

entry.title: Detecting checkout without a click handler
entry.summary: The kits page had visitors but Stripe showed no sessions. Here is how I instrumented the checkout boundary without adding click handlers to every buy button.

entry.title: What Your Literature Search Misses
entry.summary: Most missed citations aren't papers you forgot to read. They're papers in adjacent fields using different terminology for the same problem, invisible to a keyword search.

entry.title: The comment said this would break
entry.summary: The Purplelink stats endpoint read event blobs one at a time, and the code even included a comment noting it would fail at higher volume. The failure arrived through latency rather than traffic spikes.

entry.title: Producing a diff PDF for journal resubmission
entry.summary: Many journal submission portals require a diff PDF alongside a revised manuscript. Here is how a researcher uses Purplelink's LaTeX Diff tool to produce one without a local LaTeX installation.

entry.title: Why the cover letter generator doesn't see your manuscript
entry.summary: The Purplelink cover letter generator takes only your abstract, not the full manuscript. Here's the capability and privacy reasoning behind that design choice.

entry.title: What counts as a run when the tool never calls the server
entry.summary: Two Purplelink tools that compute entirely in the browser had no usage data, because instrumentation relied on intercepting backend calls. Fixing that required defining what a run actually means, and the answer differed by tool.

entry.title: What stays in a blinded manuscript
entry.summary: Double-blind peer review requires more than removing your name from the title page. Grant numbers, IRB protocols, citation prose, and named software all identify you to a reviewer who knows your field.

entry.title: What OpenAlex returns when you ask for an abstract
entry.summary: OpenAlex stores paper abstracts as inverted indexes rather than strings. Building the Daily Digest's paper fetcher surfaced this, and the reconstruction has limits.

entry.title: Running your manuscript through Paper Review
entry.summary: Paper Review scans your manuscript before submission with four adversarial passes: figure integrity, citation cross-check, a multi-persona reviewer debate, and a prioritized checklist. Here is what using it looks like from a researcher's side.

entry.title: One curation call per day
entry.summary: The Purplelink Daily Digest harvests 400-800 items daily and picks 20 to publish. Here's why the design uses a single AI curation call instead of scoring items one at a time.

entry.title: Keeping up when your research crosses fields
entry.summary: Academic researchers who work across multiple fast-moving fields have no good daily briefing built for them. Here's why the existing infrastructure falls short, and what I built to fix it.

entry.title: Where BibTeX errors actually come from
entry.summary: Most BibTeX errors don't come from researchers making mistakes. They come from the bibliography managers and export tools researchers trust to get it right.

entry.title: Getting a research paper into an LLM without losing the math
entry.summary: PDF text extraction breaks on tables and equations. Here's how a researcher uses Purplelink's PDF to Structured Data tool to get clean, LLM-ready text out of an academic paper.

entry.title: Seven free LaTeX tools, right in your browser
entry.summary: We launched a free LaTeX tools page: compile to PDF, convert to and from Word, diff two versions, validate and build BibTeX, and render equations - no account, no install, nothing stored.

entry.title: Why we built Haea on-device
entry.summary: Why Haea keeps all your health data on your iPhone - and why that decision shapes everything about how the app works.

entry.title: What GlobePin does that no other travel app does
entry.summary: Why GlobePin is different from every travel tracking app on the market - and what we built that the others missed.

entry.title: The LaTeX editor that academics actually want
entry.summary: Why existing LaTeX editors fail academic researchers - and what ModernTex does differently to serve the manuscript workflow.

entry.title: Starting Purplelink
entry.summary: Why I formed a software LLC, what I'm building with it, and the philosophy behind making software that's meant to last.
